title: Silky Egg Custard Pie
summary: A crisp blind-baked shell filled with a custard that is thickened on the stove first, so it bakes in minutes and sets silky without cracking.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, cut into 1 cm cubes
freshly grated nutmeg, plus extra to finish
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the pastry
steps.text: In a bowl or food processor, combine the 180 g flour, sugar and salt, then work in the 120 g cold butter until the largest bits are pea-size. Add the 60 ml ice-cold water and mix only until the dough clumps, with up to 15 ml more if needed. Shape into a disc, wrap and chill 1 h so the butter firms and the flour hydrates.

steps.title: Line the dish
steps.text: On a floured surface, roll the dough into a 30 cm round about 3 mm thick and lower it into the 23 cm pie dish. Trim to a 1 cm overhang, tuck the edge under and crimp, then chill 30 min. Resting stops the pastry shrinking down the sides.

steps.title: Blind bake
steps.text: With the oven at 190 °C (170 °C fan), prick the base, line it with baking paper and fill with baking beans. Bake 20 min, remove the paper and beans and give it 8-12 min more until golden all over. A fully baked shell is essential here because the custard only spends a few minutes in the oven.

steps.title: Heat the dairy
steps.text: Keep the oven at 190 °C (170 °C fan) and the shell warm. Heat the milk and cream in the saucepan over medium-low heat until steaming, about 6 min, and meanwhile whisk the eggs, sugar, cornflour, vanilla, nutmeg and salt in a bowl until smooth. The cornflour protects the eggs from curdling when the hot milk goes in.

steps.title: Thicken the custard
steps.text: Whisk the hot milk into the egg mixture in a thin stream, pour it back into the pan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring and scraping the base constantly, 6-8 min. It is ready when it reaches at least 71 °C, thickly coats the spoon and leaves a ridge when you scrape the base. Starting the set on the hob means only a short bake, so the crust never turns soggy.

steps.title: Bake briefly
steps.text: Pour the hot custard into the warm shell, grate a little nutmeg over and bake 12-15 min. Take it out when the edge is set and the centre still wobbles slightly; it firms as it cools, and overbaking makes it weep.

steps.title: Cool and chill
steps.text: Cool on the rack 2 h, then chill at least 1 h for neat wedges and cut into 8. A gradual cool keeps the surface smooth and uncracked. Keep covered in the fridge up to 3 days.

tips: Common mistake: walking away from the custard on the hob. Scrape the base constantly or it catches and turns lumpy.
A thermometer takes the guesswork out: at least 71 °C before it goes in the shell.
Grate the nutmeg fresh; it is the main flavour and fades quickly once ground.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge up to 3 days and serve cold or at cool room temperature. Custard pie does not freeze well.
